Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:

The test `testCalendarTimezoneRespected()` checks if the FastDateFormat formats a Calendar instance's datetime string respecting the Calendar's timezone. The test compares the result of SimpleDateFormat (which respects the calendar timezone) and FastDateFormat. The failure shows FastDateFormat does not respect the timezone in the Calendar when formatting the "z" (timezone name) pattern.

In the FastDateFormat class, its method format(Calendar) delegates formatting to an instance of FastDatePrinter (format(Calendar) calls printer.format(calendar)).

FastDatePrinter.format(Calendar) then calls format(Calendar, StringBuffer), which calls applyRules(Calendar, StringBuffer). applyRules iterates through formatting rules and appends their outputs to the buffer.

For timezone display, a rule like TimeZoneNameRule is responsible. Inspecting TimeZoneNameRule.appendTo shows it checks the TimeZone instance field 'zone' and uses that to decide what timezone name string to append by calling getTimeZoneDisplay.

Crucially, the TimeZoneNameRule is constructed with a TimeZone instance and caches both the standard and daylight display names for that TimeZone when the rule is created. The appendTo method only uses that cached TimeZone instance and does not consider the timezone from the calendar argument passed to it.

Therefore, even if the Calendar passed to format() has a different timezone, the timezone name displayed will always be based on the timezone set on the TimeZoneNameRule instance (which is fixed from construction time and does not update based on the Calendar parameter).

In contrast, SimpleDateFormat formats the timezone based on the timezone set on the calendar being formatted.

Thus, the core of the bug is that the FastDateFormat/FastDatePrinter caching and rule system does not dynamically respect the timezone of the Calendar passed to the format method. It uses a fixed TimeZone captured when the FastDateFormat/FastDatePrinter is instantiated.

This explains why the time and other components appear correctly formatted with the Calendar's timezone but the timezone name "z" produced is always the originating TimeZone of FastDateFormat (likely default machine timezone), leading to the observed failure.

This diagnosis matches the current bug report about FastDateFormat's "z" pattern ignoring Calendar timezone during format().

Recent unrelated bug reports about RandomStringUtils and StringUtils do not pertain to this timezone formatting issue. 

Hence, the root cause is the design of FastDatePrinter.TimeZoneNameRule's appendTo method ignoring the dynamic timezone of the passed Calendar, using only the fixed timezone from construction.

A fix would involve ensuring the timezone used for formatting the "z" pattern reflects the Calendar's timezone at format time, not an internally cached fixed TimeZone. The code would need to be changed to fetch the Calendar's timezone dynamically or avoid caching rules by fixed timezone for timezone name patterns.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
